description: Issue #839: a Heritage short alias is a built-in name at run time, exactly as illegal to declare as the canonical it spells. `define fd :n … print 999 … end` then `fd 10` used to run the learner's procedure and print `999` with no `move` event — the `setxy`/`set_xy` call-site split `docs/design-notes/0007-binding-vs-registration.md` measured, where shadowing one spelling leaves the other reaching the turtle. The runtime resolves the alias to its canonical and re-runs the same lookup rather than consulting a table of its own (`spec/conformance.md:146`, Heritage is "alternate spellings only"), so `define fd` is `ol-reserved-word` because `define forward` is. This fixture exists because a mutation deleting that alias resolution passed the ENTIRE conformance corpus — every fixture touching alias registration was `"check": true`, so nothing executed one. The unit suite caught it; the corpus did not, and the corpus is the binding artifact.

diagnostics.message: fd is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
